inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 'revenue' line carries Funds From Operations (FFO), FY26 $669.3m (Annual FY2026 p36: Underlying FFO 626.8 + trading profits 42.5). The engine's 'EBITDA' at a 100% margin is therefore FFO -- already after net finance costs, corporate costs and FFO tax -- and the capex line carries maintenance & leasing capex (FY26 $185.4m), so the engine's FCF is AFFO exactly (FY26: 669.3 - 185.4 = 483.9, ties to the reported AFFO). This is an AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity expressed on the component engine so the dashboard sliders reproduce it.
inputs.share_count_basis: Securities on issue at 30 June 2026: 1,072,589,964 (Annual FY2026 look-through NTA table; 2,975,282 bought back to 30-Jun under the 18-Feb-2026 programme). Held FLAT. The Metrics.csv FY2026 figure of 1,112.6m does not match the filing and is not used. Diluted weighted count of 1,134.7m adds 63.4m securities on exchange of the Exchangeable Notes (implied exchange price ~A$7.9); those notes sit inside borrowings and their coupon inside net finance costs, so they are treated as debt here -- out of the money at the price and at the base/bear IVs, and below the bull IV too. The on-market buyback (up to 10% to 31-Dec-2026, funded by asset sales at ~book) is roughly AFFO-per-security neutral to mildly accretive (assets sold at a ~4.9% AFFO yield on book vs securities bought at ~6.9%); not modelled, noted as bull-side upside.
inputs.net_debt_note: Set to ZERO for the model: AFFO is a post-interest, post-tax distributable flow, so it is capitalised at the cost of equity and no debt is deducted afterwards (REIT-row rule; deducting it would charge the debt twice). Balance-sheet debt is recorded in total_debt/cash for auditability only.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest received $47.9m is netted inside FFO's net finance costs (-157.4) and is therefore already inside the flow; not deducted separately.
inputs.sbc_source: Annual FY2026 statement of changes in equity, security-based payments expense $7.3m (FY25 $17.5m). Expensed inside FFO's corporate costs under the PCA AFFO definition, so sbc_pct_path is 0 -- no separate deduction, no dilution charge (share count flat).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest AFFO. Built in AUD: 10-year ACGB ~4.4% + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta ~0.95 for a 34%-geared diversified office/industrial A-REIT with a funds-management arm = ~9.6%; base 9.5%. Bull 8.75% (cap-rate compression, governance overhang clears). Bear 10.5% (governance/litigation and FUM-attrition risk priced mostly in the bear flows, with a further 1pp on the rate). Same-currency as the flows (AUD/AUD).
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS-16 lease liabilities ($80.4m) are immaterial against $5.1bn borrowings and their interest is already inside net finance costs within FFO; no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path omitted).
inputs.nci_treatment: Profit attributable to stapled security holders is the FFO basis; non-controlling interests are not material at group level. Co-investment income in pooled funds is proportionately inside FFO.
inputs.notes: MODEL: AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT / property-trust row), expressed on the owner-FCF component engine so the dashboard reproduces it. An owner-FCF DCF on statutory FCF would be meaningless: net income is dominated by IAS 40 revaluation and derivative fair-value swings (FY26 NPAT 482.2 vs FY25 136.1 on a flat AFFO), EBITDA is undefined, and statutory FCF is net of development capex/asset sales timing. Dexus straddles two rows (property trust + funds manager, 14% of FFO) but management reports one distributable measure (AFFO, PCA definition) and the funds business is too small and too impaired (infrastructure FUM under review, APAC judgment) to justify a separate multiple, so it is valued inside AFFO. NTA cross-check: look-through NTA A$8.92/security; the base IV sits ~40% below it because the book values imply only a ~4.3% AFFO yield on NTA at FY27 guidance, below any reasonable cost of equity -- the discount is the market pricing the asset-level cap rates (6.06%) against a ~9.5% equity return after 34% gearing and 28-30% of FFO absorbed by maintenance capex and incentives (average office incentives 29.9%). Anchor vintages: price 22-Sep-2026 close; balance sheet, share count and NTA all 30-Jun-2026 (Annual FY2026 released 20-Aug-2026); FY27 guidance from the same release. Metrics.csv FY2026 shares_outstanding (1,112.6m) disagrees with the filing (1,072.6m) -- flagged, not used.

engine_mapping.revenue: FFO (Underlying FFO + trading profits, net of tax)
engine_mapping.ebitda_margin_path: 100% -- the 'EBITDA' IS FFO, post net finance costs, corporate costs and FFO tax
engine_mapping.capex_pct_path: Maintenance capex + lessor works + cash incentives + rent-free incentives as % of FFO (FY26 27.7%)
engine_mapping.sbc/da/tax/wc: zero -- all already inside FFO under the PCA AFFO definition

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward judgment: long-run AFFO growth after the FY27 reset, roughly CPI-minus. Every trailing series is negative (revenue shrinking on $2.5bn of asset sales, AFFO/security -4.5% p.a. over 3 years, NTA/security -4.0% p.a. over 5 years, equity -6.7% p.a. over 3 years) and describes the cap-rate de-rating and asset recycling of FY22-FY26, not the forward run-rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.7%/-4.4%) is revaluation-driven and EPS CAGR is undefined (FY23/FY24 statutory losses were fair-value writedowns). fcf_* CAGRs are the AFFO-per-security series, not reported FCF (reported FCF 544->472 over 3 years is asset-sale timing).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted vs reported FCF divergence is not meaningful here: SBC ($7.3m) is 1.5% of AFFO and is expensed inside FFO.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY27 FFO -11.8% with capex at 30% of FFO gives AFFO $413m = 38.5 cps on 1,072.6m securities, the midpoint of the 37.5-39.5 cps guidance (trading profits ~nil vs $42.5m, performance fees immaterial, higher net finance costs incl. Atlassian Central interest no longer capitalised, lower FUM-under-review contribution). FY28 +1% as hedge roll-off (WACD 4.2%->4.7%) offsets leasing momentum; FY29-FY31 +2.5-3% as prime-CBD supply stays tight and Atlassian Central/Waterfront Brisbane rent comes on; 2.5% thereafter. Capex glides from 30% to 28% of FFO as incentives normalise from the FY26 29.9% average; never below the FY25-26 27.7-28.5% range.
base.terminal_rationale: Terminal growth 2.0% (CPI-minus: office rents grow with CPI but 28% of FFO is recurring maintenance/incentive leakage). Gordon multiple at 9.5%/2.0% is 13.6x terminal AFFO (~7.3% yield), under the 14x cap.

bull.growth_rates_rationale: FY27 at the top of guidance (~39.6 cps: FFO -10.5%, capex 29%). FY28-FY30 +4-5% as trading profits and DWPF performance fees return, cap rates compress, the Boral logistics partnership and third-party raisings (~$2bn FY26) rebuild management-operations FFO, and the buyback at ~0.62x NTA adds ~1% per 5% of the register. Incentives normalise to 26% of FFO. Cost of equity 8.75% and 2.5% terminal growth (Gordon 16.4x, capped at 16x ~6.25% yield) capture partial convergence toward NTA; even so the bull IV stays below the A$8.92 NTA and below the ~A$7.9 exchangeable-note exchange price, so no note dilution.

bear.growth_rates_rationale: FY27 at the bottom of guidance (37.2 cps: FFO -13.5%, capex 31%). FY28 -6% and FY29 -2%: the infrastructure-FUM strategic review ends in redemptions/liquidation (~$35m of fees, ~5% of FFO), the APAC appeal fails and Dexus wears adverse costs and a forced sale of the Dexus Bloc's airport stake, the Healthcare fund redemption queue grows, and hedges roll into a 5%+ cost of debt. Recovery limited to 1.5% p.a. with incentives stuck at 30% of FFO (Melbourne CBD vacancy ~20%). Cost of equity 10.5%, terminal growth 1.0%, 12x cap (~8.3% yield).

scenario_narratives.base: AFFO resets to the FY27 guidance midpoint (38.5 cps) as trading profits and performance fees drop out and finance costs rise, then grows 2.5-3% p.a. from FY29 on prime-CBD leasing momentum and completed developments, with maintenance capex and incentives absorbing ~28% of FFO. Capitalised at a 9.5% AUD cost of equity with 2.0% terminal growth (13.6x terminal AFFO). The funds-management franchise stabilises but does not re-rate; the buyback is executed and roughly per-security neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY27 lands at the top of guidance and FFO grows 4-5% p.a. through FY30 as cap rates compress, DWPF performance fees and trading profits return, third-party capital raising (~$2bn in FY26) and the Boral logistics estate rebuild the management-operations line, and incentives normalise to 26% of FFO. The governance overhang clears on appeal and the discount to NTA narrows: 8.75% cost of equity, 2.5% terminal growth, 16x cap. Value still sits below the A$8.92 NTA.
scenario_narratives.bear: The APAC 'material irremediable breach' judgment stands, the infrastructure-FUM review ends in redemptions, the Healthcare fund queue grows and the funds-management annuity shrinks; higher debt costs as hedges roll and 30% incentive leakage push AFFO down to ~31 cps by FY29 before a 1.5% recovery. 10.5% cost of equity, 1.0% terminal growth, 12x cap. Distribution of 37 cps would be uncovered and cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 25% default to 30% and bull cut to 20%: an unresolved court finding of a material irremediable breach against the manager, a strategic review over $7.3bn of FUM with no decision yet, FY27 AFFO guided down 12-18%, and a ten-year TSR of 0.2% p.a. are evidence of execution risk that the flows alone do not fully carry. The balance sheet (A-/A3, 33.4% gearing, $2.5bn liquidity) is not the risk, so bear is not weighted higher than 30%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Dexus is valued on what it can distribute -- AFFO under the Property Council definition, after maintenance capex and leasing incentives -- capitalised at an AUD cost of equity with no further debt deduction. Net tangible assets (A$8.92/security) are a cross-check, not the anchor: book cap rates of ~6.1% imply a ~4.3% AFFO yield on NTA at FY27 guidance, below any reasonable cost of equity, which is why the securities have traded at a 30-40% discount to book for years and why the base IV sits below NTA. The value case rests on whether the FY27 reset is a floor (base/bull) or the first leg of a funds-management unwind (bear).
key_risks_to_valuation: APAC / Melbourne Airport litigation: appeal outcome, adverse costs, forced sale of the ~$4.5bn Dexus Bloc stake and the reputational cost to third-party capital raising
Infrastructure FUM strategic review ($7.3bn, ~$35m fees) and Healthcare fund redemption queue -- funds-management FFO already -17% in FY26
Office demand: 54-57% of FFO from office with national CBD vacancy 14-16% and Melbourne ~20%; incentives at ~30% of face rent absorb 28-30% of FFO
Cost of debt rising as hedges roll (4.2% -> 4.7% in one half); each 50bp on $5.1bn look-through borrowings is ~5% of AFFO
Cap-rate direction: a reversal of the FY26 stabilisation would hit NTA, gearing and the buyback capacity simultaneously
Exchangeable Notes (63.4m securities, ~A$7.9 exchange) become dilutive only above the bull IV; treated as debt here
